Grade 7 Accelerated · Unit 3 · Lesson 9 — Writing Small Numbers in Scientific Notation3

Notes

I. Negative powers of ten name the decimal places

10010-110-210-310-410-5
10.10.010.0010.00010.00001

  1. A negative exponent puts the 1 in that decimal place: 10-4 is a 1 in the fourth place.
Grade 7 Accelerated · Unit 3 · Lesson 9 — Writing Small Numbers in Scientific Notation4

Notes

II. Small numbers in scientific notation

  1. The coefficient is still at least 1 and less than 10. The exponent is negative for a number less than 1.
  2. The exponent is how many places the point moves: 0.0000672 → 6.72 is five places right, so 10-5.
Grade 7 Accelerated · Unit 3 · Lesson 9 — Writing Small Numbers in Scientific Notation5

Notes

III. How many times larger — or smaller?

  1. Divide the coefficients. Divide the powers of 10 — subtract the exponents. Multiply the results.
  2. Which is bigger, 10-5 or 10-8? The one with the larger exponent: −5 > −8, so 10-5.
Grade 7 Accelerated · Unit 3 · Lesson 9 — Writing Small Numbers in Scientific Notation6
